To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high-performing virtual project teams are characterized by a) a shared understanding of the project, b) a high degree of trust, c) the use of technology to support communication and coordination, and d) a high degree (relative to low-performing teams) of proactive use of technology.
the project teams' and management team's use of communication processes and technology, and their ability to adapt to the virtual setting, influenced their ability to manage the project.

high-performing project teams and their managers are more likely to engage in proactive behaviors, such as using technology to manage processes and to develop relational ties, and to be more responsive to the needs of the project team members.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the communication processes engaged by virtual project teams in the course of their work, as well as the communication processes engaged to manage them.

the management of virtual project teams is a complex process, and the management of the management team is an additional complexity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
virtual project management is not just about technology, but about people and their relationships with each other.
virtual project management is possible and successful, but requires careful planning and attention to the unique challenges of virtual project management.
the project team and management team processes were interrelated and interdependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the management of a project team is a critical factor in determining its success.
project management practices and virtual team dynamics are intertwined, and both are critical to project success.
the communication content in the virtual teams and the management team is rich with lessons for both working in virtual teams and managing virtual teams.
